title: A Maryland Man Carried Cocaine in Cakes
central_question: Gildo Ricci, 69, flew into Dulles from Bogota in April 2024 with a suitcase of sweets; a customs officer's knife would not go into one cake, and under the top layer was a foil-wrapped brick: 2.07 kg of cocaine in his cakes and soup mix. A backpack in the suitcase held $7,750, all counterfeit. A federal jury convicted him in January 2025. Which was worse: the cocaine cake or the fake cash?

pronounce.$7,750: seven thousand, seven hundred and fifty dollars

content_notes: Tone: dry and ironic; the joke is on the scheme (a cake a knife could not cut, a backpack of fake cash), never on his age or nationality. Gildo Ricci was convicted by a federal jury (Alexandria, January 2025) and is named by the US Attorney's Office and the press, so he is named; he is drawn ONLY as a dark rim-lit silhouette (NOT A LIKENESS), standing across an inspection table and in a dock, with no flag, costume or national marker. The cake is a generic pink-frosted layer cake (its look is not reported); the brick is a plain foil block. The customs officer and the judge are generic figures with no badge, patch, seal, flag, agency name or insignia; no weapon; the knife points only into the cake. The inspection room and court are illustrations, not reported places; no airline, airport sign or logo is copied. The inventory tag is our own typed graphic, not a CBP form. The affidavit wording on the fun-fact card is carried by FOX 5 DC, The Washington Times and the release. No dialogue is invented. Not used: the single-source 18-month sentence and appeal, the 20-year maximum, the word 'child's'. Facts verified 2026-10-26.

claims.text: Gildo Ricci, 69, carried cakes and soup mixes holding cocaine into Washington Dulles from Bogota on 25 April 2024; a federal jury convicted him of possession with intent to distribute. Narration: 'A traveler carried cocaine inside his cakes.' (FFXnow's word: 'Dulles Airport traveler'). Headline 'A COCAINE CAKE / THE KNIFE COULDN'T CUT'. The conviction is to possession: the reel says 'carried', never 'baked' or 'hid'.
STATISTIC: 2.07 kg (about 4.5 lb) of cocaine in all, in his cakes and soup-mix packets. Narration: '2 kilos of it. Even in the soup mix.' Counter '2.07 KG' in the court scene.

Customs officers sent him to secondary inspection; one cake was unusually heavy; the officer probed it with a knife, which failed to penetrate the cake; under the top layer was a foil-wrapped brick. Narration (gotcha): 'Then a customs officer's knife wouldn't go in.' Callout 'A FOIL-WRAPPED BRICK', sub 'Under the top layer'. The cake's look and the brick's size are not reported: drawn generic.

He arrived at Washington Dulles International Airport on 25 April 2024 (about 6:45 am, per the FBI affidavit) on a flight from Bogota, Colombia. Label 'DULLES AIRPORT · 25 APR 2024', sub 'Flight from Bogota · secondary inspection'.

He is Gildo Ricci, 69, a Peruvian citizen and lawful permanent resident of the US, living in Rockville, Maryland; convicted by a federal jury and named by the US Attorney's Office and the press. Narration: 'His name was Gildo Ricci. He was 69.' Label 'GILDO RICCI · 69 · ROCKVILLE, MD', sub 'Convicted · silhouette, not a likeness'. Drawn only as a silhouette.

He flew into Washington Dulles from Bogota, Colombia, landing at about 6:45 am (FBI affidavit, quoted by FOX 5 DC and FFXnow). Narration: 'Into Dulles from Bogota, about a quarter to seven.' Label 'BOGOTA → DULLES · ABOUT 6:45 AM'.

Officers found several dessert and food items in his luggage, such as chocolate candies, cakes and soup mixes. Narration: 'His bags held chocolates, cakes and soup mix.' Label 'CHOCOLATES · CAKES · SOUP MIX'.
Inside one of his suitcases was a backpack holding $7,750. Narration: 'But there was a backpack too.' (The release says a child's backpack; the reel does not use the word.)

The backpack held $7,750 in cash. Narration: 'Inside, $7,750.' (spoken: seven thousand, seven hundred and fifty dollars) Evidence close-up: our own typed inventory tag 'ITEM: BACKPACK · CASH: $7,750' (no real form imitated).
The $7,750 was later determined to be counterfeit. Narration: 'All of it fake.' Stamp 'COUNTERFEIT' on the tag.
He went to trial before a federal jury in Alexandria, Virginia (he did not plead guilty). Narration (second re-hook): 'Then he took it to a jury.'

In January 2025 a federal jury in Alexandria convicted him of possession with intent to distribute cocaine. Narration: 'A federal jury convicted him.' Label 'FEDERAL COURT · ALEXANDRIA, VA', sub 'Convicted · January 2025'. The sentence (18 months, Virginia Lawyers Weekly only) is not used.
The counter: 2.07 KG, cocaine in the cakes and soup mix (as K_weight).

FUN FACT (wording as reported, from the FBI affidavit quoted by FOX 5 DC and The Washington Times, and in the release): the knife 'failed to penetrate the cake'. Card 'THE AFFIDAVIT: THE KNIFE / "FAILED TO PENETRATE THE CAKE"'.
Each of the cakes contained cocaine (as did the soup-mix packets). Narration (callback): 'Every cake in his suitcase held cocaine.' Callout 'EVERY CAKE', sub 'And the soup mix'.
